verdict.rationale: The packet sequence shows peer-to-peer RPC endpoint-mapper traffic, an immediate dynamic-port exchange carrying substantial client payload, and then a new connection from the target peer to the same TCP/80 destination already used by the initiating peer. That tightly ordered cross-host pattern is most consistent with remote execution followed by shared command-and-control activity, although packet telemetry alone cannot confirm the RPC interface, service creation, process execution, or destination role.

acceptable_alternatives.rationale: Suspicious is fully equivalent because O1-O3 (P000157-P000159, P000171-P000173, P000182, P000185, P000190, P000209) establish an RPC exchange with large client payloads but do not decode the interface or operation, while O4-O5 (P000003, P000156, P000246, P000249) do not establish the role of 10.24.9.50. Escalation is required because endpoint attribution and authorization remain unavailable.

observations.desc: WKS-4471 and WKS-4472 sensors recorded a TCP exchange from 10.24.8.21:56607 to 10.24.8.22:135 beginning at 2020-09-20 16:16:56.519.
Nine milliseconds later, both sensors recorded a TCP session from 10.24.8.21:56608 to 10.24.8.22:49726.
Target-side packets on the 49726 session include multiple client-to-server payload segments, including 1418, 543, 220, and 1182 bytes, with server-to-client response segments also present.
10.24.8.21 exchanged TCP/80 packets with 10.24.9.50 before and during the peer RPC sequence.
At 16:17:01.658, 10.24.8.22 initiated a separate TCP connection to 10.24.9.50:80 and sent a 201-byte payload after the handshake.

inferences.desc: The TCP/135 exchange followed immediately by a session to TCP/49726 is consistent with RPC endpoint mapping and a related dynamic-port RPC operation.

The amount and direction of dynamic-port payload are consistent with a state-changing remote administration operation, including possible service creation, but the RPC interface and operation are not decoded.
The shared TCP/80 destination and timing are consistent with a newly established beacon or command-and-control channel on 10.24.8.22 after remote execution.

investigations.desc: Obtain endpoint process, service, authentication, and file telemetry from both peers for 16:16:56-16:17:02 to identify the socket owners and any service creation or execution.
Decode the TCP/135 and TCP/49726 packet payloads to identify the RPC interface UUID and operation numbers.
Determine the asset role and ownership of 10.24.9.50 and inspect the TCP/80 application content and historical connection cadence from both peers.
Compare peer-to-peer RPC activity against the environment baseline and check for approved administration at the observed time.

unknowns.desc: The processes and accounts responsible for the observed network sessions are unknown because endpoint telemetry is not provided.
The RPC interface, requested operations, and whether a service was created or executed are unknown.
The role, ownership, and application content of 10.24.9.50:80 are unknown; the private address must not be assumed to be external.
